Ali's Thesis · Operational Forecasting

Forecast Model Comparison

Pooled best results across four experiments on the same daily ERP series: deep-learning forecasters (MLP, CNN, LSTM) in both an untuned baseline and a per-target hyperparameter-tuned configuration (units, learning rate, dropout tuned separately for Sales, Cost and Margin, with a days-to-month-end calendar feature), plus two zero-training agent-reasoning variants (plain direct prompting and in-context direct prompting). Ranked by MASE, where below 1.00 beats a naive last-value forecast.

Reading this dashboard. Each cell shows the best result actually achieved, so the untuned DL baseline appears wherever it outperformed its tuned counterpart. MASE is the ranking metric: it is scale-free (comparable across Cost, Margin and Sales, which differ greatly in magnitude) and MASE < 1.00 means the model beats a naive “repeat the last value” forecast; above 1.00 is worse than doing nothing.

Reading this. Full grid search: all 24 combinations of units × learning rate × dropout trained and validated together, instead of locking in one setting at a time the way the old sequential/OFAT (one-factor-at-a-time) search did in 9 trainings. Each mini-chart shows, for every value of that setting, the best MASE achievable across all combinations of the other two (marginalising them out) — the filled point/bar is the value used by the single true joint-optimal 24-combination winner. More expensive (24 trainings instead of 9) but can catch settings that only work well together, which a sequential search can miss by construction. Ranked by validation MASE, computed per target (not averaged across Cost/Margin/Sales).
